egress.terms: Free and unmetered. Public file access returns 303 -> a presigned S3 URL (dvn-cloud-iqss.s3.amazonaws.com) valid 3600s; S3 honours Range requests. No egress pricing exists anywhere in the product. Probe: GET /api/access/datafile/11685194 -L -H 'Range: bytes=0-1023' -> 303 then HTTP 206, Content-Range: bytes 0-1023/21269528, Server: AmazonS3.

tooling: Native REST API v6.10.1 (live: GET /api/info/version -> {"version":"6.10.1"}); SWORD v2 deposit; OAI-PMH harvest; S3 direct-upload API for files >2.5 GB (docs: 'This option can handle files >300GB'). Python client pyDataverse; R package dataverse. No rclone backend, but a REST loop is trivial (~15 lines) and the platform is a well-documented Invenio-free Java stack.
chaining: Unlimited Dataverse Collections per account (Harvard: 9,755 collections / 306,011 datasets exist, anyone may create one). x 1 TB per collection. 20 collections = 20 TB in one account; 20 accounts = 400 TB. Also multiplies per *dataset* rather than per collection if the 1 TB is read as a guidance number, since no per-dataset quota is enforced on the root collection.
